evidence.title: Online anti-Muslim backlash collides with different reality in South Africa

occurrences.checkable_against: Al Jazeera interview recording or transcript with Thembisa Fakude
occurrences.quote_span: “It’s true, but it’s not only South Africa. This is global … In South Africa, yes, it’s true. You find that there will always be bigots, you know, and others will be, you know, ultra-Zulu nationalist or ultra-nationalist.”
occurrences.speaker: Thembisa Fakude
occurrences.subject: anti-Muslim rhetoric in South Africa

occurrences.checkable_against: Al Jazeera interview recording or transcript with Moulana Sulaiman Ravat
occurrences.quote_span: “I don’t think we can go to the other extreme. We must understand that there are certain global political realities, and the Islamophobia project aligns with those global agendas. And therefore, if we become complacent or nonchalant about it, what people are exposed to online could start impacting their psyche and how they think.”
occurrences.speaker: Moulana Sulaiman Ravat
occurrences.subject: anti-Muslim rhetoric in South Africa

occurrences.checkable_against: Al Jazeera interview recording or transcript with Khethukuthula Dlame
occurrences.quote_span: “The move to orchestrated hate towards Muslims is not at a community level. If you’re looking at people when they’re mobilising, it’s not people from the villages. It is people in cities and in hostels.”
occurrences.speaker: Khethukuthula Dlame
occurrences.subject: anti-Muslim rhetoric in South Africa

occurrences.checkable_against: Archived social-media post
occurrences.quote_span: Another claimed: “Most foreigners in South Africa are Muslim and if you look most countries experiencing war are Muslim countries not Christian ones.”
occurrences.speaker: social media post author
occurrences.subject: anti-Muslim rhetoric in South Africa

occurrences.checkable_against: Al Jazeera interview recording or transcript with Khethukuthula Dlame
occurrences.quote_span: “In these communities, there’s harmony and respect. People really respect my religion,” he told Al Jazeera, standing alongside his grandfather’s gravesite.
occurrences.speaker: Khethukuthula Dlame
occurrences.subject: anti-Muslim rhetoric in South Africa

occurrences.checkable_against: Al Jazeera interview recording or transcript with Khethukuthula Dlame
occurrences.quote_span: “The people behind this understand the flash points. If you really want to cause divisions, you use tribal rhetoric and the people you mobilise and agitate are in hostels because the living conditions are not good.”
occurrences.speaker: Khethukuthula Dlame
occurrences.subject: anti-Muslim rhetoric in South Africa

occurrences.checkable_against: Archived South African social-media posts
occurrences.quote_span: Others have accused Muslims of “targeting poverty-stricken communities and converting them to Islam”.
occurrences.speaker: social media post authors
occurrences.subject: anti-Muslim rhetoric in South Africa

occurrences.checkable_against: Archived social-media post and Gift of the Givers records
occurrences.quote_span: One social media post complained that humanitarian organisation Gift of the Givers had been “getting on our nerves with their insistence on pushing their Muslim beliefs in South Africa”.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: anti-Muslim rhetoric in South Africa

occurrences.checkable_against: Archived South African social-media posts and platform records
occurrences.quote_span: Posts have accused Muslims of attempting to take over South Africa, questioned their belonging in the country and accused Muslim organisations of using charity and poverty to convert Black South Africans to Islam.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: anti-Muslim rhetoric in South Africa

occurrences.checkable_against: Al Jazeera interview and Samukelisiwe Ngubane's testimony
occurrences.quote_span: For Samukelisiwe Ngubane, her first encounters with Muslims came through Indian shopkeepers in a nearby town.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: anti-Muslim rhetoric in South Africa

occurrences.checkable_against: Al Jazeera interview recording or transcript with Samukelisiwe Ngubane
occurrences.quote_span: “We have never had a problem. Some people are curious about what they [Muslims] do, but there have been no problems,” she told Al Jazeera.
occurrences.speaker: Samukelisiwe Ngubane
occurrences.subject: anti-Muslim rhetoric in South Africa

occurrences.checkable_against: Ngubane family statements and funeral records
occurrences.quote_span: When he died, his family honoured his wishes.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: anti-Muslim rhetoric in South Africa

occurrences.checkable_against: Al Jazeera reporting or recording of the Nquthu community meeting
occurrences.quote_span: Earlier, at a community meeting, Dlame explained that Muslims, too, believe that Jesus was a prophet of God.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: anti-Muslim rhetoric in South Africa

occurrences.checkable_against: Al Jazeera interview recording or transcript with Thembisa Fakude
occurrences.quote_span: “I’ll argue that there is no widespread or any orchestrated, well-planned Islamophobia directed towards Muslims. We don’t have that.”
occurrences.speaker: Thembisa Fakude
occurrences.subject: anti-Muslim rhetoric in South Africa

occurrences.checkable_against: Future South African anti-Muslim incident and public-attitude records
occurrences.quote_span: “Better be proactive than reactive. It’s a global reality. It has been for the last 20 years. And the fact that it could increase in South Africa and could have serious consequences, you could argue, is unlikely but not impossible.”
occurrences.speaker: Moulana Sulaiman Ravat
occurrences.subject: anti-Muslim rhetoric in South Africa

occurrences.checkable_against: Al Jazeera interview recording or transcript with Moulana Sulaiman Ravat
occurrences.quote_span: “They don’t speak the language any more. They are as South African as anyone else.”
occurrences.speaker: Moulana Sulaiman Ravat
occurrences.subject: anti-Muslim rhetoric in South Africa

occurrences.checkable_against: Al Jazeera interview recording or transcript with Thembisa Fakude and cited allegations
occurrences.quote_span: Fakude also argues that Muslim communities need to confront allegations of racism and exploitative labour practices within their own ranks rather than characterising every criticism as religious prejudice.
occurrences.speaker: Thembisa Fakude
occurrences.subject: anti-Muslim rhetoric in South Africa

occurrences.checkable_against: South African xenophobic violence incident records and research
occurrences.quote_span: South Africa has repeatedly experienced outbreaks of xenophobic violence since the end of apartheid, with migrants from elsewhere on the African continent often bearing the brunt.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: anti-Muslim rhetoric in South Africa

occurrences.checkable_against: Nquthu community interviews and Ngubane funeral reporting
occurrences.quote_span: For a community largely unfamiliar with Islamic burial practices, the funeral was a novelty. But it wasn’t a controversy.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: anti-Muslim rhetoric in South Africa

occurrences.checkable_against: Al Jazeera reporting or recording of the Nquthu community meeting
occurrences.quote_span: Ordinary villagers listened attentively and joined in Zulu melodies in praise of God.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: anti-Muslim rhetoric in South Africa

occurrences.checkable_against: Al Jazeera interview recording or transcript with Thembisa Fakude
occurrences.quote_span: “It is a storm in a teacup. And I think what’s concerning me is this othering by Muslims wanting to position themselves as victims and taking this course by themselves. It’s extremely dangerous.”
occurrences.speaker: Thembisa Fakude
occurrences.subject: anti-Muslim rhetoric in South Africa

occurrences.checkable_against: Al Jazeera interview recording or transcript with Moulana Sulaiman Ravat
occurrences.quote_span: “I would think I would say they are deeply religious and deeply patriotic, and there is no contradiction between the two.”
occurrences.speaker: Moulana Sulaiman Ravat
occurrences.subject: anti-Muslim rhetoric in South Africa

occurrences.checkable_against: Al Jazeera reporting and Nquthu community interviews
occurrences.quote_span: Dlame, now 26 and one of only a handful of Muslims known in his village, is familiar enough to his neighbours that his Islamic clothing is a source of teasing rather than hostility.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: anti-Muslim rhetoric in South Africa

occurrences.checkable_against: South African social-media content and media-monitoring records from 2026
occurrences.quote_span: In recent months, anti-Muslim rhetoric has become more visible online, intersecting with a heated national debate about immigration and anti-migrant movements.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: anti-Muslim rhetoric in South Africa

occurrences.checkable_against: Ravat family and genealogical records
occurrences.quote_span: His own children, he said, are fifth-generation South African Muslims of Indian heritage.
occurrences.speaker: Moulana Sulaiman Ravat
occurrences.subject: anti-Muslim rhetoric in South Africa

occurrences.checkable_against: Al Jazeera interview recording or transcript with Moulana Sulaiman Ravat
occurrences.quote_span: Ravat argues that Muslim identity is sometimes being presented as evidence that a person is somehow less South African.
occurrences.speaker: Moulana Sulaiman Ravat
occurrences.subject: anti-Muslim rhetoric in South Africa

occurrences.checkable_against: Al Jazeera interview recording or transcript with Moulana Sulaiman Ravat
occurrences.quote_span: “At the same time, I think on the ground, South Africans in the main are not Islamophobic, and there’s a variety of indicators to substantiate that.”
occurrences.speaker: Moulana Sulaiman Ravat
occurrences.subject: anti-Muslim rhetoric in South Africa
